newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on bleak exports, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on bleak exports, technicals.

text.p: The lowest weekly export inspections figure since 1982 and weak technical indicators drove CBOT wheat futures lower on Monday, traders said.

USDA Monday said export inspections for the week ended December 26 totalled a paltry 4.5 million bushels, the lowest since 1982 when USDA began keeping computerized records and far below last week's total of 13.5 million bushels.
While that week included the Christmas Day holiday, traders said the figure was still far below expectations and confirmed persistent belief that U.S. wheat was overvalued relative to world prices.
U.S. soft red winter wheat on Monday was selling for $159.35 per ton, FOB U.S. Gulf, export sources said. Argentine wheat was selling for $144.00 per ton for January delivery.
Still, traders noted some optimism that Pakistan would look to U.S. supplies to fill at least part of their 600,000-tonne wheat tender.
"There's a good chance we'll see some of that," one trader said, noting that the tender was for white wheat and U.S. supplies of that grade were readily available.
Wheat closed 7-1/2 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower with March down 7-1/2 at $3.82.
Commercial buying on the breaks limited losses and added to suspicions that Pakistan would buy U.S. supplies.
Cargill Inc bought at least 1.2 million bushels of March in early dealings, traders said.
Refco Inc sold about 1.5 million bushels of March, and the Chicago Corporation bought about 1 million March, traders said. Volume was light.
